To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of cellular tissues are often complex, that they are often best described by individual-based models, that they are best understood by considering the interaction between cell proliferation and phenotype, that these models can be used to predict long-term equilibria and transient dynamics in tissues, that they can be used to assess the efficacy of combination therapy, and that they can be useful for interpreting biopsy specimens.
“Cellular interactions can profoundly affect the dynamics of cellular systems and the resulting dynamics are often non-intuitive.”

(1) the dynamics of cellular tissues are often more complex and more interesting than those of simple populations of identical cells, (2) the complexity of these dynamics can be understood and quantified using game theoretic methods, and (3) the results of such analysis can be used to improve our understanding of cancer and to improve cancer therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how cellular interactions influence the dynamics of cellular proliferation and the evolution of cellular phenotype.
understanding the dynamics and control of cellular populations in which cell phenotype can be altered by cell-cell interaction.
the application of mathematical methods to problems in cell biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
game theory has been used to model the behavior of populations of cells in which there is interaction between cells.
the mathematical methods of game theory can provide valuable insight into the dynamics of cellular systems.

the application of game theory to cancer research has provided new insights into the dynamics of tumor cell populations and has led to the development of new methods for the analysis of tumor growth and response to treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that spatial heterogeneity and phenotypic switching can have a dramatic effect on the long-term behavior of a population, and that these effects may be difficult to predict based on the behavior of a spatially homogeneous, nonswitching population.
we are developing mathematical models to understand the dynamics of cellular interactions in cancer.
we are trying to model the dynamics and spatial heterogeneity of tumor growth and response to therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of a tissue are strongly influenced by the interactions between its component cells.
the dynamics of heterogeneous tissues can be quite complex and difficult to predict.
the dynamics of a cellular population are strongly influenced by the spatial structure and the nature of the cell-to-cell interactions.
